cards.title: One lap decides the whole race
cards.text: 22 cars, three rounds: 6 out after the first, 6 after the second, and ten left to fight for the grid that shapes everything the race can become.

cards.title: Hamilton takes it
cards.text: By 0.009s over Russell. Less time than a blink.

cards.title: Out before it got serious
cards.text: Albon (P16), Alonso (P17), Hirakawa (P18), Stroll (P19), Perez (P20), Bottas (P21).

cards.title: So close to the top ten
cards.text: Hulkenberg (P10), Colapinto (P11), Piastri (P12), Bortoleto (P13), Bearman (P14), Sainz (P15).

cards.title: Lawson has no place in the result
cards.text: He set times all the way to Q3, and the classification still leaves him out. The timing feed records that, not why.

cards.title: Lawson loses all his times
cards.text: Disqualified from the session: a technical infringement. Everybody behind him moves up a place.

cards.title: 12 laps thrown in the bin
cards.text: In qualifying a deleted lap can be the difference between Q3 and going home early.

cards.title: Gasly, Colapinto and Hadjar were quickest through the trap: 351 km/h
cards.text: Top speed says as much about wing level and the tow from the car ahead as it does about the engine.

cards.title: Nobody owned the whole lap
cards.text: The quickest sectors of the session were split between three drivers, so the ideal lap was never actually driven.

cards.title: Yellow flags out 2 times, and the session stopped once
cards.text: A red flag stops the session and sends everybody back to the pits.

cards.title: How the race starts
cards.text: P1 Hamilton · P2 Russell · P3 Leclerc · P4 Antonelli · P5 Verstappen · P6 Norris
bullets: Verstappen qualified P4 and starts P5, 1 place further back
The grid is not the qualifying order. A penalty moves a car back, whether for something on track or for a new engine, and everybody behind it moves up
